Since your freelance turnover is £8,000 for the 2025-26 tax year, you won't need to use Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax, as the threshold of £30,000 starts from 6 April 2027. However, being paid under PAYE does not automatically exempt you from needing to file a Self Assessment tax return if your total income exceeds certain limits or if you have other untaxed income.

Would you like to know more about your Self Assessment obligations?

sources.title: PAYE employment plus additional income
sources.excerpt: Being taxed under PAYE does not automatically mean you have no Self Assessment obligations. Additional untaxed income, self-employment, property income or other criteria can still mean you need to file a return. Check GOV.UK ‘who must send a tax return’.

sources.title: MTD Income Tax £30,000 threshold starts 6 April 2027
sources.excerpt: If your qualifying income is more than £30,000 for the 2025-26 tax year (2025 to 2026), you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027. This is not April 2026. April 2026 applies only to the higher £50,000 qualifying-income band (based on 2024-25). Qualifying income is turnover/gross self-employment and property income before expenses, not profit after expenses.

sources.title: What qualifying income means for MTD
sources.excerpt: Qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax is total income from self-employment and property before expenses (also described as turnover/gross income), based on the relevant Self Assessment return. Employment (PAYE), dividends, State Pension and private pensions do not count towards qualifying income. Do not confuse turnover with profit.
